title: Perform basic routine operations in a defined hydroponic context

lessons.title: Working in a hydroponic tunnel
lessons.html:
What hydroponics is

In hydroponics, plants grow without soil. Their roots sit in a bag of growing medium, like coir or sawdust, or in channels of water. The plants get water and food from a nutrient solution: water with fertiliser mixed in. Pipes and drippers bring the solution to each plant. Most hydroponic crops grow in a tunnel or greenhouse. Common crops are tomatoes, cucumbers, peppers, lettuce and herbs.

Hygiene first

Pests and diseases spread fast in a tunnel because plants are close together. Before you go in:

  1. Wash your hands with soap.
  2. Step in the foot bath at the door.
  3. Close the door behind you. Open doors let insects in.
  4. Do not bring food, smoke or spit inside.
  5. Do not go into the tunnel after working in another tunnel with sick plants, unless your supervisor says you may.

Parts you will work with

  • Tank – holds the water or nutrient solution.
  • Pump and timer – push the solution to the plants at set times.
  • Pipes and drippers – carry the solution to each plant.
  • Bags or channels – hold the plants and roots.
  • Drain – carries away extra water.

Stay safe

  • Do not touch the pump, timer or electrics unless you are trained. Report any wet plug or broken cable.
  • Wear gloves when you handle fertiliser.
  • The tunnel can get very hot. Drink water often and rest in the shade at breaks.
  • Do not climb on bags or wires to reach plants. Use the trolley or step the supervisor gives you.

lessons.title: Daily tasks and what to report
lessons.html:
Your daily tasks

Your supervisor will give you tasks for the day. Common tasks are:

Checking the drippers

  1. Walk slowly along each row while the system is running.
  2. Look at every plant. Is the dripper in the bag? Is water coming out?
  3. Push loose drippers back into the bag.
  4. If a dripper is blocked, tell your supervisor or clean it as you were shown.

Looking after the plants

  • Training – twist tomato and cucumber stems gently around the string so they grow up straight.
  • Side-shooting – pinch off small side shoots on tomatoes, as you were shown, so the plant puts its energy into fruit.
  • Removing old leaves – take off yellow or dead leaves at the bottom of the plant.
  • Harvesting – pick fruit at the colour and size your supervisor shows you. Handle gently. Put fruit in clean crates, not on the floor.

Keeping the tunnel clean

  • Put all leaves, shoots and bad fruit in the waste bin or bag, not on the floor. Old plant parts on the floor spread disease.
  • Sweep paths.
  • Keep tools clean.

What to report at once

You seeTell your supervisor
Plants wiltingPlants may not be getting water
No water from drippersPump, timer or tank problem
Water leaking or poolingBroken pipe or dripper
Small white flies, spots on leaves, holes, sticky leavesPests or disease
Brown, slimy rootsRoot disease
Door left open or torn plasticPests can get in

Tell the supervisor which row and which plant. You can tie a piece of tape on the string to mark it.

Key points

  • Hydroponic plants get water and food from a nutrient solution, not soil.
  • Wash hands, use the foot bath and close the door.
  • Check every dripper and push loose ones back.
  • Keep plant waste off the floor.
  • Report wilting, no water, leaks, pests and torn plastic at once.

quiz.question: Where do hydroponic plants get their food from?
Why should you step in the foot bath before going into the tunnel?

options.text: To clean your boots for the shop
To stop pests and diseases coming in on your shoes

quiz.question: You see a dripper lying outside the bag. What should you do?

options.text: Push it back into the bag

quiz.question: Where should old leaves and bad fruit go?

options.text: In the waste bin or bag

quiz.question: Many plants in a row are wilting. What could this mean?

options.text: The plants are getting too much light
The plants may not be getting water
The plants are ready to harvest

quiz.question: You should close the tunnel door behind you to keep insects out.
Any worker may fix the pump and electrics.
